work.title: BRIGHT EDIT
work.subtitle: 品牌信息与内容手册
work.framework: marketing: Copy and proof boundary / distinct native A4 document layout
work.scope: Fictional editorial campaign. No real product endorsement, conversion result, customer testimonial or unsupported performance claim.

pages.title: Make the message easy to understand.
pages.lead: BRIGHT EDIT is a fictional messaging handbook for an imagined creative collection. It separates a clear invitation from a claim that would need evidence.
pages.body: The aim is to practise coherent language across a headline, short description and next action. The artwork suggests tone; it does not demonstrate product performance.

pages.question: What should a reader understand after the first paragraph?

pages.title: Read the message system.
pages.lead: The handbook moves from audience question to message, proof boundary, tone, content formats and review. It is a document for writers, not a live campaign dashboard.
pages.body: Pages 3–5 define the intended conversation. Pages 6–8 adapt it to formats and review claims. Pages 9–10 prepare a handoff and retain the source boundary.

pages.title: Use an audience question, not a stereotype.
pages.lead: Imagine a reader who wants to understand a creative idea quickly. This is a writing premise, not a researched persona or statement about a demographic group.
pages.body: Do not invent personal characteristics or needs. Frame the task as a question the copy should answer, such as What is this and why might I explore it?

pages.question: Which reader question can the text actually answer?

pages.title: Write one central message.
pages.lead: Suggested fictional message: Explore a clearer way to collect creative references. It describes an invitation rather than a guaranteed benefit.
pages.body: Keep the promise smaller than the missing evidence. Avoid claims such as proven to improve results when no relevant study, product or measurement exists.

pages.question: Which word makes the message stronger than its support?

pages.title: Attach a proof boundary.
pages.lead: A photograph, illustration or attractive sentence is not proof of effectiveness. This case provides no customer results, test data or testimonial.
pages.body: A useful proof note distinguishes an available demonstration from an outcome claim. Where a source is missing, keep the statement provisional or remove it.

pages.question: What evidence would this sentence require?

pages.title: Use a recognisable voice.
pages.lead: The proposed voice is clear, curious and specific. That is an editorial direction, not a claim that every audience will respond positively.
pages.body: Prefer concrete nouns and short explanations. A sentence can be warm without exaggeration, and confident without implying certainty about an untested outcome.

pages.question: Which sentence could be made more concrete?

pages.title: Adapt without changing the promise.
pages.lead: A brochure paragraph, a short caption and an email opening can share one message while differing in length. The underlying evidence boundary should not disappear in shorter copy.
pages.body: Write the long version first, then remove repetition rather than qualifications that affect meaning. Keep a link or note for context where the format allows it.

pages.title: Review the call to action.
pages.lead: A fictional call to action might invite a reader to view the concept or ask a question. It should not imply an available product, guaranteed offer or completed transaction.
pages.body: The example contains no live checkout, price or promotion. State what the reader can genuinely do in the actual context before publishing a real campaign.

pages.title: Hand over the message set.
pages.lead: Share the headline, description, evidence note, tone guidance and unresolved questions together. A contributor should not have to guess which claim has been checked.
pages.body: Label approved wording only after a real responsible process exists. In this exercise, all messages remain fictional drafts for discussion.

pages.title: Check claims before publishing.
pages.lead: Review every factual statement, implied outcome and quotation. Remove invented results and clearly identify visual inspiration.
pages.body: This handbook does not supply a legal review or a compliance guarantee. A real campaign requires appropriate source checks and responsible editorial review.
